title: Flag orders from customers who ordered before
persona: Runs a small clothing store and writes short, practical English. Wants the packing staff to notice a returning customer and add a thank-you note. Does not care how it is done as long as the flag is right.
opening: flag orders from customers who ordered before

facts.what counts as the same customer: the same phone number or the same email, either one is enough
facts.the time window: they ordered before within the last 90 days
facts.where the flag shows: on the order, in my orders list
facts.what happens to a flagged order: nothing automatic, the staff just see it
facts.older orders: past orders too if that is easy, otherwise only new ones

success: a rule or a worked-out flag over the store's orders marks the repeat ones
it matches a customer by phone or by email, either one
it asks about the time window or states it as 90 days
the plan is said in plain words before anything is built, with no field names or types
ends by asking whether to build
must_not: a rule that writes a value into every order on a schedule
jargon such as "boolean" or "set_fields" in what the owner reads
